text: Milk is soured with a starter (and sometimes a little pepsin) for about 8 hours until it forms a curd block, which is cut, warmed a little to drain and pressed. The sources opened do not name the starter species.

steps.note: Standardised to the wanted fat first; classic acid-set curd is often from skimmed milk.
In the acid-rennet kind rennet (chymosin) or pepsin is added with the starter.
Traditionally in free-hanging bags; industrially cut with strings, squeezed, cooled and packed.

processing.text: Species are not named. The acid-rennet kind adds rennet or pepsin with the starter; the curd is then cut, warmed to 40-45 °C and drained.
